title: Roy Rogers
paragraphs: A family Western adventure series starring Roy Rogers, often joined by Dale Evans and familiar supporting characters in stories mixing action, humor, music, and frontier justice.

Family-oriented singing-cowboy Western starring Roy Rogers, frequently with Dale Evans and later Pat Brady, mixing adventure, humor, music and contemporary technology in a stylized modern West. Frozen GRH snapshot contains 96 playable objects from 1945-1955, including three undated archive items.

GRH documents the program through Mutual first run (November 21, 1944 to May 8, 1945) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], NBC run (October 5, 1946 to March 29, 1947) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Mutual transcribed Western era (1948-08 to May 13, 1951) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and NBC final run (October 5, 1951 to July 21, 1955) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|roy-rogers|Roy Rogers]] (performer on 78 recordings), Dale Evans (performer on 75 recordings), Art Ballinger (announcer on 60 recordings), Art Rush (producer on 55 recordings, performer on 5 recordings, and production supervisor on 5 recordings), Milton Charles (performer on 34 recordings and music on 20 recordings), Frank Hemingway (performer on 53 recordings), and Pat Brady (performer on 43 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include western song and musical performance, ranching and cattle, outlaws and criminal gangs, outlaws and banditry, frontier law and justice, and mining and gold.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Singing-cowboy radio format, Early transcribed network production, Sponsor premiums and youth marketing, and Radio/television overlap.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (61 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (50 shared credited people), [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] (41 shared credited people), [[show|wild-bill-hickok|Wild Bill Hickok]] (39 shared credited people), and [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]] (39 shared credited people).
